# Set up
1. Load the tidyverse library. 
2. Load the billboard data.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data("billboard")
```

3. Describe the dataset. 
```{r}
summary(billboard)
# billboard is a dataset that has 76 weeks worth of top radio songs, including weekly rankings of songs that hit the Billboard Top 100. artist: the name of the musical artist or group. track: the title of the song. date.entered: the date the song first entered the Billboard Top 100. wk1 to wk76: Numeric columns showing the song's rank during each week (with NA for weeks the song was no longer on the chart).
```

4. Print the column names from this dataset. 
```{r}
colnames(billboard)
```

5. Print the first 5 entries in the dataset.
```{r}
head(billboard, 5)
```


# Practice
1. Create a subset of data that has Jay-Z as the only artist. How many songs are in it?
```{r}
billboardJayZ <- subset(billboard, artist == "Jay-Z")
nrow(billboardJayZ)
# 5 songs
```

2. In the original dataset, use filter to find information about the song "All the small things." What was the highest position (i.e. lowest number) this song reached on the billboard 100? 
```{r}
summary(billboard |> filter(track == "All The Small Things"))
#6
```

3. Create a subset of data for songs Tim McGraw sang. Summarize the data for wk 1.
```{r}
billboardMcgraw <- subset(billboard, artist == "McGraw, Tim")
summary(billboardMcgraw$wk1)
```

4. Create a function that can be used to determine if Britney Spears sang the song. 
```{r}
for(i in 1:length(billboard$artist)){
  if(billboard$artist[i]== "Spears, Britney"){
    print(billboard$track[i])
  }
}
```

5. Test your function on the billboard data. Save the results to a new column called "wasItBritney"
```{r}
billboard$wasItBritney <- NA
for(i in 1:length(billboard$artist)){
  if(billboard$artist[i]== "Spears, Britney"){
    billboard$wasItBritney[i] <- TRUE
  } else{
    billboard$wasItBritney[i] <- FALSE
  }
}
```

6. Use a for loop to determine if a song placed 50 or below or placed above 50 during the first week. 
```{r}
billboard$week1Rank <- NA
for(i in 1:nrow(billboard)){
  if(billboard$wk1[i] <= 50){
    billboard$week1Rank[i] <- "50 or below"
  } else{
    billboard$week1Rank[i] <- "above 50"
  }
}
```

7. Use an if else statement to determine the same information as you obtained with the for loop.
```{r}
billboard$week1RankJR<- ifelse(billboard$wk1 <= 50, "50 or below", "above 50")
```

8. Compare your results in 6 and 7. 
```{r}
#They produce the same results. the if else without the for loop was much quicker to write
```
